reason: The cited evidence shows that aging can form strengthening precipitates in other high-entropy alloy systems (E1, E2) and that Orowan pinning is a valid mechanism (E2), but none of the evidence involves the TiVNbTa alloy or demonstrates precipitate stability and strengthening at 1273 K. The key premise that this specific alloy will form stable, strengthening precipitates under the proposed treatment is unsupported.
premises: Aging can produce secondary precipitates (e.g., Laves or B2) in refractory high-entropy alloys.
Such precipitates can impede dislocation motion via Orowan pinning.
Thermally stable precipitates can delay creep and recovery at high temperature.
Precipitate strengthening can increase yield strength at elevated temperature (1273 K).
The specific TiVNbTa alloy system can form such precipitates under the proposed heat treatment.
